name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 303 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 24% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 303 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 24 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Violent clashes continue in Manipur as rival Kuki-Zo and Naga groups engaged in gunfights, killing three Kuki-Zo volunteers and prompting large rallies demanding the SoO agreement’s abrogation and the return of displaced families. Security forces recovered the bodies of two abducted Kuki men and later arrested three militants in Imphal, while a joint operation found two missing Kuki villagers dead. In Kashmir, a convoy of the Darbar Move was escorted through Ramban under tight security and a 13-year-old boy was killed and seven people injured in a road mishap. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Voldelige sammenstøt fortsetter i Manipur ettersom rivaliserende Kuki-Zo‑ og Naga-grupper har engasjert seg i skyting, der tre Kuki-Zo-frivillige ble drept og store demonstrasjoner har krevd opphevelse av SoO-avtalen og tilbakeføring av fordrevede familier. Sikkerhetsstyrker fant kroppene til to bortførte Kuki-menn og arresterte senere tre militante i Imphal, mens en felles operasjon avdekket to savnede Kuki-bønder døde. I Kashmir ble en konvoi med Darbar-flyttingen eskortert gjennom Ramban under tett sikkerhet, og en 13‑år gammel gutt ble drept og syv personer såret i en trafikkulykke. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
